ROOT_CAUSE:
The order was written to *classify* the 22 non-navigation misses; reading their own frames turned up a defect instead, and one with a single mechanism.

Measured on 2026-10-02: 20 of the day's 92 failures were `SELECT_RESOURCE`, the largest block of non-navigation misses. Their `before` frames read `page=MAP`, `resource_search_open=True`, a **beast** tab selected (`BEAST` / `GIANT_BEAST`) and `resource_tab_kinds` naming only the beast tabs. On four of those steps' own frames the production geometry layer returns:

    semantic.selected_resource  -> None
    semantic.resource_tab_offset -> None
    semantic.anchored_tab_kind   -> None
    resource_cell_center_norm(MEAT/WOOD/COAL/IRON) -> None

The resolver for `RESOURCE_DYNAMIC` is one line -- `resource_cell_center_norm(resource)` -- which needs `resource_tab_offset`. And the runtime's only recovery for "the cell is off-screen" was gated on `resource_tab_offset is not None` as well, because the scroll amount comes from `resource_tab_swipe_for`, which needs the same offset. So when the offset could not be resolved the loop could **neither tap nor scroll**: nothing was attempted, the step was refused in 0.11-0.16 s, `state_after` was empty (the step never reached the device), it happened **twice in a row** ~6 s apart, and each pair was the last thing its episode did. 21 of the 21 such failures in the window were the last step of their episode or followed by another failure; **not one was followed by a success**, which is what distinguishes this from the camp first-tap cluster closed last round.

That is a failure shape with no recovery at all, and the recovery was gated on the very quantity that was missing.

REMAINING_ISSUE:
Three.

(a) **The fix converts an immediate refusal into up to three bounded swipes and then a refusal.** It does not guarantee the outcome. The mechanism it relies on is that scrolling brings the gatherable cells into view, at which point the reviewed cell templates match and `resource_tab_offset` resolves -- the same path the offset-present case already used. If the templates do not match those cells on the live client, the step will still refuse, only later and after three swipes. The live reading is what decides that, and it has not happened yet.

(b) **`resource_tab_order` is a constant and the client's strip order has drifted before** -- the project's own note on `read_resource_tab_labels` says the order drifts between client versions. My direction rule reads that constant. If it has drifted, the swipe goes the wrong way: bounded (one pitch, `max_scroll_attempts`), re-observed, and still strictly better than the guaranteed refusal, but worth knowing. A direction derived from the *visible labels' own x positions* would not depend on the constant; that is the more durable rule and I did not have a measurement to build it from this round.

(c) **The remaining 14 non-navigation misses are still only classified as NOT_A_NAVIGATION_ACTION**: SELECT_BEAST_TARGET_MAMMOTH 10 and TRY_ORDINARY_CONTROL 3 (plus SEARCH_RESOURCE 1). `SELECT_BEAST_TARGET_MAMMOTH` has `decision_reason = verified_visible_mammoth_target` while `failure_type = SEMANTIC_TARGET_NOT_VERIFIED` -- the decision layer says the target is visible and the resolver cannot find it on the same frame, which is a different mechanism from this one and is exactly the locator-layer attribution the order originally asked for.
